chapters.title: AI Assistant
intro: This chapter is for agents and supervisors who use AI help in their daily work.
It covers the **AI Assistant** page and the **AI** tab on a ticket. It also covers AI reply drafts and AI proposals.

sections.title: What the AI can do for you
sections.intro: The AI reads your tickets and knowledge base. It suggests summaries, replies, classifications and next steps. A person stays in charge: you review every suggestion before it reaches a customer.

list: The **AI Assistant** page answers questions about your data, searches by meaning, lists AI proposals and shows unusual ticket volume.
The **AI** tab on a ticket summarises it and drafts replies, classifications and articles.
**Draft with AI** in the reply editor writes a first reply for you.

rows: Use the **AI** tab, **Draft with AI**, **Semantic search** and, with analytics access, **Ask analytics**.
**Supervisor monitoring (live queues, agent status)**, team analytics or AI settings

blocks.warning: AI text can be wrong. Always read a draft and check its sources before you send it.

blocks.note: The demo uses a built-in offline AI. Your administrator may connect another AI service and set a monthly budget.

sections.title: The AI Assistant page
sections.intro: Select **AI Assistant** in the main menu. The page opens on the first tab you may use.

rows: Answers a question about your tickets with a chart and a table.
Finds tickets and articles that mean the same as your words, even with different wording.
Lists actions that AI agents suggest. You approve, reject or revert them.
Shows days with unusually many tickets for a product, version, customer or category.

blocks.note: Administrators also see **AI settings** at the top right. It opens the AI configuration pages.

sections.title: Ask a question about your ticket data
sections.intro: Ask in plain words, such as “Open tickets per agent”. The AI turns your question into a report.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** and **View personal dashboards and reports** permissions.
steps: Select **AI Assistant**, then **Ask analytics**.
Enter your question in the question box.
Select **Ask**. You can also select one of the example questions below the box.
Check the line under the answer title. It shows how the question was understood.
Read the chart and the **Results** table.
sections.result: The answer shows the metric, the breakdown and the period. If nothing matches, **No matching tickets** appears.

blocks.caption: Ask analytics with an example question and its answer.
blocks.alt: Ask analytics tab with numbered highlights on the tabs, the question box, the example questions, the understood question and the results

callouts: The tabs of the AI Assistant page.
The question box and the **Ask** button.
Example questions. Select one to ask it at once.
How the question was understood: **Metric**, **Breakdown**, **Period**, **Order** and **Parsed by**.

blocks.tip: Select a bar or a row to open the matching tickets in the ticket list.
Select **Show structured intent** to see exactly what the question was turned into.

sections.title: What you can ask
sections.intro: Questions work best when they name one measure, one breakdown and a period.

rows: Tickets created, open or resolved, SLA violations, resolution time, first-response time, CSAT, and reopened, escalated or frustrated tickets.
Customer, product, category, priority, channel, department, agent, team, status, or over time.
Words such as this month, this quarter, or the last 30 or 90 days.

blocks.note: The answers cover only the tickets you may see. The AI never changes any data.

sections.title: Search tickets and articles by meaning
sections.intro: Describe a problem in your own words. The search finds similar tickets and articles, even when they use other words.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.
steps: Select **AI Assistant**, then **Semantic search**.
Describe the problem in the search box. Use at least two characters.
Choose where to search: **Everything**, **Tickets** or **Knowledge articles**.
Select **Search**.
Select a title to open the ticket or article.
sections.result: The results are listed with the best match first. Each result shows its type, status, a short extract and a relevance bar.

blocks.caption: Semantic search results for a description of an export problem.
blocks.alt: Semantic search tab with numbered highlights on the search box, the scope options and the first result

callouts: The search box and the **Search** button.
A result with its type, title, status, extract and relevance.

blocks.tip: Under a ticket result, select **AI insights for this ticket** to open the full-page AI assistant for it.

sections.title: How AI proposals work
sections.intro: AI agents watch new tickets. They suggest actions such as a category, a priority, tags, a note or a reply. Each suggestion is a proposal. Most proposals wait for a person to approve them.

list: Each proposal has a risk level: **Low risk**, **Medium risk** or **High risk**.
Each proposal shows a confidence bar, the AI agent's name and the reason for the suggestion.
Your administrator may let some low-risk actions apply automatically. Such cards say **applied automatically**.
A proposal expires after 14 days if nobody decides.

rows: Waiting for review. The **Waiting for review** filter shows these.
The change was made on the ticket.
A person undid an applied change.
The change could not be made. The card shows why.

columns: What happens when you approve it
rows: The ticket fields change. You can revert these later.
The message is sent to the customer under your name. You cannot undo it.
A note is added to the ticket.
Records that you approved handling the request. The AI never takes a financial, account or contract action.

sections.title: Review an AI proposal
sections.intro: Check what the AI suggests, then approve or reject it.
prerequisites: You have the **Approve, apply and revert AI-proposed actions** permission.
steps: Select **AI Assistant**, then **Proposals**. The list shows proposals waiting for review.
To narrow the list, choose a **Status**, **Risk** or **Action**, or enter text in **Search**.
Read the proposed change and the reason under it.
To see the ticket, select the ticket number on the card.
Select **Approve & apply**, or select **Reject**.
If a confirmation appears, read it and select **Approve & apply** again.
sections.result: The card shows the new status and who decided. A message confirms the action.

blocks.caption: The Proposals tab with all statuses shown.
blocks.alt: Proposals tab with numbered highlights on the counters, the filters, a card's risk and status badges and its confidence bar

callouts: Counters for proposals waiting, high-risk proposals waiting and applied proposals.
The risk and status of a proposal.
The AI's confidence in the proposal.

blocks.warning: An approved reply is sent to the customer under your name at once. Read it carefully first.

sections.title: Undo an applied AI action
sections.intro: Undo a category, priority or tag change that the AI made.
prerequisites: You have the **Approve, apply and revert AI-proposed actions** permission.
The proposal is **Applied** and can be reverted. Sent messages cannot be reverted.
steps: Select **AI Assistant**, then **Proposals**.
In **Status**, choose **Applied**.
On the card, select **Revert**.
Select **Revert** again to confirm.
sections.result: The fields the AI changed go back to their earlier values. Changes that people made since then are kept. The card shows **Reverted**.

sections.title: Watch for unusual ticket volume
sections.intro: The **Anomalies** tab flags days with far more tickets than usual. Each hour, the app compares each day with the previous 28 days. It checks every product, version, customer and category.
prerequisites: You have supervisor monitoring, team analytics or AI settings permission.
steps: Select **AI Assistant**, then **Anomalies**.
In **Period**, choose **Last 7 days**, **Last 30 days** or **Last 90 days**.
In **Status**, choose **Open**, **Acknowledged** or **Dismissed**, or leave it empty for all.
Compare the bars in **Volume vs. typical day**. Select a bar to see the tickets of that day.
In the **Anomaly alerts** table, select **Acknowledge** when you are handling a spike. Select **Dismiss** when it needs no action.
sections.result: The alert shows its new status. If no spike was found, **No unusual volume** appears.

rows: The product, version, customer or category that had the spike.
The number of tickets on that day.
The average for a day over the previous 28 days.

sections.title: The AI tab on a ticket
sections.intro: Open a ticket and select the **AI** tab. On a narrow screen, select **Ticket details** (the sliders button) first. The tab loads the sentiment and the expected resolution time at once. The other parts run when you select their button.

blocks.caption: The AI tab of a ticket with sentiment and expected resolution.
blocks.alt: AI tab with Summary, Sentiment, Expected resolution, Classification, Suggested reply, Similar and duplicates, Likely root cause and Knowledge article

rows: A short summary, the current status and pending actions. The summary is saved on the ticket.
The customer's mood: **Positive**, **Neutral**, **Negative** or **Frustrated**. A dot shows each customer message.
The typical time to resolve similar tickets, with a range and an expected date.
Suggested category, product, priority and department. See [Apply AI classification suggestions](#apply-ai-classification).
A reply based on articles and resolved tickets. See [Draft a reply with AI](#draft-reply-ai).
Possible duplicates and similar resolved tickets.
Likely causes, based on similar resolved tickets.
A draft article from this ticket. See [Draft an article from a ticket](#kb-draft-from-ticket).
The proposals for this ticket. **Run agents** asks the AI agents to check it again.

blocks.note: When a customer is **Frustrated**, the tab says: acknowledge the impact and give a concrete next step.

sections.title: Summarise a ticket
sections.intro: Get a short summary of a long conversation before you take over a ticket.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.
steps: Open the ticket and its **AI** tab.
Under **Summary**, select **Summarize**. If a summary exists, the button says **Refresh**.
sections.result: The summary appears with the current status and any pending actions. The last line shows when it was made.

sections.title: Apply AI classification suggestions
sections.intro: Let the AI suggest the category, product, priority and department. Apply only the values you agree with.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.
To apply values, you also need the **Edit ticket fields** permission.
steps: Open the ticket and its **AI** tab.
Under **Classification**, select **Suggest**.

steps.text: Check each suggestion. A crossed-out value shows the current value, and the arrow shows the suggested one.
steps.caption: Classification suggestions. Ticked values are applied; values with a check mark already match.
steps.alt: Classification section with category and department suggestions, confidence bars and Apply selected

steps: Tick the suggestions you want to apply. Clear the others.
Select **Apply selected**.
sections.result: The message **Classification applied** appears, and the ticket fields change.

blocks.tip: The bar next to each value shows the AI's confidence. Be careful with short or red bars.

sections.title: Draft a reply with AI
sections.intro: The AI writes a reply from your knowledge base and similar resolved tickets. You review it, then send it from the reply editor.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.
steps: Open the ticket and its **AI** tab.
Optionally, under **Suggested reply**, enter instructions, such as `mention the 8.0.1 upgrade`.
Select **Draft reply**.

steps.text: Check the badge. **Grounded in knowledge** means the draft uses your articles or resolved tickets.
steps.caption: A drafted reply with its badge, confidence and numbered sources.
steps.alt: Suggested reply with Grounded in knowledge badge, draft text, sources and Insert into composer, Copy, Helpful and Not helpful

steps: Read the draft and the sources listed under it.
Select **Insert into composer**. Or select **Copy** to copy the text.
In the reply editor, remove the [1], [2] source markers and edit the text.
Send the reply as usual.
sections.result: The reply reaches the customer under your name.

blocks.warning: **Not grounded — review carefully** means no matching article or resolved ticket was found. Check every fact before you send it.

blocks.tip: Select **Redraft** for a new version. Select the thumbs-up or thumbs-down button to tell the AI whether the draft helped.

sections.title: Draft a reply from the reply editor
sections.intro: You can also start an AI draft without opening the AI tab.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.
steps: Open the ticket.
Select **Reply** to open the reply editor.
In the editor toolbar, select **Draft with AI**.
Read the message that appears. It says how many sources the draft used.
Edit the draft and remove the source markers.
Send the reply as usual.
sections.result: The draft is inserted into the reply editor. If the editor was empty, the draft fills it.

sections.title: Find similar and duplicate tickets
sections.intro: Check whether the customer already reported the same problem. See how similar problems were solved.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.
steps: Open the ticket and its **AI** tab.
Under **Similar & duplicates**, select **Find**.
Under **Possible duplicates**, check the open tickets from the same contact or customer.
Under **Similar resolved tickets**, read how each one was resolved and its root cause.
To merge a duplicate, select **Merge this ticket into** and the ticket number. Confirm with **Merge**.
sections.result: The lists show matches with a similarity bar. After a merge, this ticket is closed as a duplicate.

blocks.warning: A merge moves the conversation, attachments and watchers to the other ticket. You need the **Merge tickets** permission.

sections.title: Find the likely root cause
sections.intro: See what usually caused this kind of problem before.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.
steps: Open the ticket and its **AI** tab.
Under **Likely root cause**, select **Analyse**.
Read the causes. Each has a likelihood bar and an explanation.
Under **Evidence**, select a ticket number to open a similar ticket.
sections.result: The causes are listed with the most likely first. The last line shows how many tickets were considered.

sections.title: Ask the AI agents to check a ticket again
sections.intro: AI agents usually run when a ticket arrives. Run them again after the ticket changes.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** and **Edit ticket fields** permissions.
steps: Open the ticket and its **AI** tab.
Under **AI proposals**, select **Run agents**.
Read the new proposals. Approve or reject them as in [Review an AI proposal](#review-ai-proposal).
sections.result: The message **AI agents finished** says how many agents ran and how many proposals they made.

sections.title: The full-page AI assistant for one ticket
sections.intro: Links on the **Proposals**, **Semantic search** and **Anomalies** tabs open a full page for one ticket. It shows the ticket facts, a reply box and the same AI parts as the **AI** tab.

blocks.caption: The full-page AI assistant with the ticket facts, the reply box and the AI parts.
blocks.alt: AI assistant page for a ticket with ticket facts, Reply with AI draft and Send reply, and AI sections on the right

list: To open another ticket, enter its number in **Ticket #** at the top right and select **Open**.
Select **Ticket** at the top right to open the ticket itself.
In **Reply**, select **AI draft** to fill the reply box with a draft.
Remove the [n] source markers. Then select **Send reply**, or press [[Ctrl+Enter]].

sections.title: AI badges and scores
sections.intro: These badges and bars appear on AI results.

rows: The draft is based on your articles or resolved tickets.
No source was found. The text may contain guesses.
How sure the AI is. Green is high, amber is medium and red is low.
The expected resolution time is based on few similar tickets.
How close a ticket or article is to this one.
The customer seems upset. Respond with care.
The sentiment has not been worked out yet.

troubleshooting.problem: An AI button shows **AI is turned off for this organisation**.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to turn it on in **AI settings**.

troubleshooting.problem: An AI part says the feature is turned off.
troubleshooting.cause: An administrator turned off this AI feature.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to turn the feature on in **AI settings**.

troubleshooting.problem: The message **This AI feature is not included in your plan** appears.
troubleshooting.cause: Your subscription does not include the feature.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your administrator about upgrading the plan.

troubleshooting.problem: The message **Your role cannot use this AI feature** appears.
troubleshooting.cause: Your role is not allowed to use that AI feature.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to change your role.

troubleshooting.problem: An AI request fails with a message about the monthly budget.
troubleshooting.cause: The workspace has used its AI budget for this month.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to raise the budget, or wait for the next month.

troubleshooting.problem: The **AI** tab or the **AI Assistant** menu item is missing.
troubleshooting.cause: You lack the AI permission, or your plan has no AI.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator for the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.

troubleshooting.cause: No tickets match the question in that period.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask about a longer period, such as the last 90 days.

troubleshooting.problem: **Approve & apply**, **Reject** and **Revert** are missing on proposals.
troubleshooting.cause: You can view proposals but not decide them.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator for the **Approve, apply and revert AI-proposed actions** permission.

faq.q: Does the AI send anything to customers by itself?
faq.a: Only if your administrator allows automatic replies for approved situations. Otherwise every reply waits for a person. Automatic replies are blocked for critical tickets and frustrated customers.

faq.q: Can I undo an AI change?
faq.a: You can revert category, product, department, priority and tag changes on the **Proposals** tab. Messages that were sent cannot be undone.

faq.q: Where do the AI's answers come from?
faq.a: From your published articles and resolved tickets. A reply draft lists its sources under the text.
Nobody approved or rejected it within 14 days.

glossary.definition: An action that an AI agent suggests for a ticket, such as a new priority or a reply. A person approves or rejects it.
An automatic AI helper that checks tickets and makes proposals, such as the triage assistant.
Said of an AI draft that is based on your own articles or resolved tickets.
A search that finds items with the same meaning as your words, even when the wording differs.
A day with far more tickets than usual for a product, version, customer or category.
The customer's mood as the AI reads it: positive, neutral, negative or frustrated.
How sure the AI is about a suggestion, shown as a bar or a percentage.
